abstract: Peroxisomes are dynamic metabolic organelles whose dysfunction results in severe diseases. The homeostasis of peroxisomes is also ensured through pexophagy, a type of selective autophagy targeting these organelles. Pexophagy can be activated by several stressors, such as starvation, mTOR inhibition, and iron deficiency. However, the regulatory mechanisms underlying pexophagy are poorly characterized. Here, we identify a novel regulatory axis of iron deficiency-induced pexophagy, which preferentially engages GABARAP among the mATG8 family members. Comparative analysis of the mATG8 interactomes reveals that upon iron depletion, GABARAP selectively interacts with the tumor suppressor complex FLCN/FNIP1 triggering the activation of the autophagy and lysosome transcription factors TFEB and TFE3, thus promoting efficient cargo degradation. Our findings thus identify the GABARAP-FLCN/FNIP1 axis as a molecular sensor that bridges iron deficiency and TFEB/TFE3 activation to prime pexophagy execution.
